headline: This change emails a 40% discount to inactive users after every publish, including people who unsubscribed.
what_changed: Every time the app is published, a win-back email offering 40% off is sent to inactive users.
A user counts as inactive if they have not been active for 30 days, or have never been active.
The email uses the subject "We miss you! 40% off your next course" and the discount code COMEBACK40.
The send runs as an extra step after the normal publish step. If it fails, the publish is reported as failed.
No screens, payments or existing customer features were changed.

risks.title: Emails go to people who already unsubscribed
risks.explanation: The customer list records when someone unsubscribes, but the new send step never checks that record. People who asked to stop getting emails will receive a marketing offer anyway. This breaks anti-spam and privacy rules such as CAN-SPAM (US) and GDPR (EU), and can lead to complaints and fines. Fix: skip every user who has an unsubscribe date before sending.

risks.title: Same customers get the offer again on every publish
risks.explanation: The send step is attached to the after-publish command, so it runs each time the app is published. It keeps no record of who was already emailed, so inactive users can get the 40% offer again and again, sometimes within days. Fix: record each send and skip anyone already emailed, or remove this step from the publish command and run it once on purpose.

risks.title: Marketing email has no unsubscribe link or company address
risks.explanation: The email body contains only a greeting and the discount code. It has no unsubscribe link and no postal address, which marketing emails normally need under anti-spam laws. Customers who want out have no simple way to opt out from this email.

risks.title: One failed email stops the run and causes repeats
risks.explanation: The loop has no error handling. If the mail service rejects one email, the whole run stops, the publish step fails, and a retry would send emails again to the people who were already reached. This is a realistic outcome given that mail services sometimes fail.

questions_for_developer: Can you make the send skip every user who has an unsubscribe date, and confirm that before it sends?
Can you stop this email from being sent on every publish, so each customer gets it only once, and record who has been sent it?
Is the code COMEBACK40 real, limited to one use per customer, and set to expire? Who approved a 40% discount for this list?
Should people who have never used the app (no activity date at all) get a discount email? Do we have their consent to email them?
Can you add an unsubscribe link and our company postal address to the email, as anti-spam laws require?
good_news: The change is small and contained, touching only two files.
The mail sending key is kept in a setting rather than written into the code.
The customer list already has an unsubscribe field, so the fix is simple to make.
